# CQ

> CQ is plain C plus one header, `CQ.h`, with four primitives. The compiler `cqcc` (clang -O1, then
> the LLVM pass `cq-lower`) turns every operation on quantum data into reversible circuits behind a
> backend interface. Write ordinary C; do not write gates.

Full manual: docs/MANUAL.md. Normative rules: spec/CONSTRUCTION_RULES.md. User surface: spec/CQ.h.
Backend contract: spec/BACKEND_ABI.md. Worked programs: examples/grover/grover.c, examples/dicke/dicke.c.

## The whole API

    cq_theta(&x, angle);    // Ry(angle) on every qubit of x, in place. x: any integer or float l-value. Makes x quantum.
    cq_phi(angle);          // multiply the amplitude of the current branch by e^(i*angle)
    r = cq_measure(x);      // measure x, return the classical outcome (same type as x)
    cq_invert_begin(); ...; cq_invert_end();   // the enclosed code runs as its adjoint
    CQ_K(fn, k)             // file scope: loop cutoff for function fn
    CQ_K2(fn, bytes)        // file scope: byte bound for fn's allocations of quantum size

`CQ.h` is included automatically by `cqcc`. Angles are `double`, in radians, and classical.

## Rules for writing CQ

- There is no qubit type, no register object, no gate list, no circuit builder. Do not invent
  `qubit`, `qreg`, `cq_h`, `cq_x`, `cq_cnot`, `cq_alloc` or any other name: they do not exist.
- A value is quantum iff it derives from a `cq_theta` result (through arithmetic, memory, calls,
  pointers). Everything else is classical host code.
- Uniform superposition of an n-bit integer: start at 0, `cq_theta(&x, M_PI / 2)`.
- One qubit: `bool q = 0;`. A register of individually addressed qubits: `bool q[N];`, not the
  bits of a wide integer.
- Controlled Ry: `if (c) cq_theta(&q, a);`. Doubly controlled: `if (c && d) cq_theta(&q, a);`.
- CNOT: `t ^= c;` on `bool`s. X: `q = !q;` or `q ^= 1;`.
- Phase oracle: `if (pred(x)) cq_phi(M_PI);`. `pred` is ordinary C, `math.h` included.
- `x += y`, `x ^= y`, `x += 3` on a quantum `x` that is not read afterwards are in place: one gate on
  x's register, no extra qubits for the result. `x -= y` and `if (c) x += y` are not.
- Do not uncompute by hand. Temporaries of an expression or a call are cleared by the compiler.
- Adjoint of a block: wrap it in `cq_invert_begin()` / `cq_invert_end()`.
- `if` on a quantum condition runs both arms; phases, rotations and stores are controlled by it.
- A loop whose exit test reads quantum data runs exactly K trips (default 4). Set K to cover the
  largest trip count in superposition: `CQ_K(fn, k)` or `-cq-k=fn=k`. Prefer classical loop bounds.
- `printf` of a quantum value is deferred to the end of the run: the value is measured, then printed.
- `cq_measure` inside a quantum branch measures unconditionally.
- Library calls on quantum values work (`sqrt(x)`, `sin(x)`, `strlen(s)`, `sprintf`), and are
  expensive: a `double` operation is thousands of gates. Use the narrowest integer type that fits.
- C undefined behaviour is still undefined (division by 0, shift by the width, out-of-bounds).
- x86-64 macOS and LLVM 19 only.

## Minimal program

    #include <math.h>
    #include <stdio.h>
    int main(void) {
        unsigned char x = 0;
        cq_theta(&x, M_PI / 2);                    /* all 256 values */
        for (int r = 0; r < 12; r++) {             /* classical loop */
            if (sqrt(x) == 12.0) cq_phi(M_PI);     /* oracle */
            cq_invert_begin(); cq_theta(&x, M_PI / 2); cq_invert_end();
            if (x != 0) cq_phi(M_PI);              /* diffusion */
            cq_theta(&x, M_PI / 2);
        }
        printf("%d\n", x);                         /* measured at the end: 144 */
        return 0;
    }

## Commands

    cqcc -S prog.c -o prog.lowered.ll                  # lowered LLVM IR, no backend needed
    cqcc -S --cq-check [--cq-entry fn] prog.c          # compare with the C program: exit 0 pass, 1 differs, 2 undecided
    cqcc prog.c -lcq_backend -lcq_gates_count -o prog  # executable; CQ_COUNT=file ./prog counts gates, depth, qubits
    cqcc prog.c -lcq_backend -lcq_gates_trace -o prog  # CQ_TRACE=file ./prog writes the circuit
    cqcc -cq-k=fn=16 -cq-k-default=8 ...               # loop cutoffs
    cqcc --save-temps DIR ...                          # keep linked.ll (pass input) and lowered.ll
    cqcc --help                                        # every option

From a checkout without `cqcc` on the PATH: `driver/cqcc`. The backend libraries come from
https://github.com/SoerenWilkening/opcode_quantum_operations (see README.md).

## Reading failures

- `cq: internal error: ...`: a compiler bug, never a property of the program. There is no
  "unsupported" diagnostic. Keep `linked.ll` and report it; do not rewrite the program to dodge it
  without saying so.
- `--cq-check` exit 1: the lowering differs from C on the printed input. Check first whether a
  quantum-exit loop needs more than K trips.
- Undefined `cq_template_f*` at link: build `softfloat/` (docs/MANUAL.md) or use a backend with floats.
- Backend aborts on a wide quantum address: index arrays by a narrow quantum value; avoid walking
  a quantum pointer.
